description: The unit of retrieval: a piece of a document small enough to embed, rank and quote, stored with its source, offsets and metadata.
Windows of a fixed number of characters or tokens, stepping by size minus overlap. Simple and predictable, blind to sentences and structure.
Split on the coarsest separator (paragraphs) first and recurse with finer ones (lines, sentences, words) only where a piece is still too big, then merge pieces back up to the size.
Chunking along the document's own structure (Markdown or HTML headings, code symbols, clauses), so no chunk crosses a section and each keeps its heading path.
Text repeated at the start of the next chunk so content near a boundary appears whole in at least one chunk. Typically 10 to 20% of the size.
The titles of a chunk's section and its ancestors, such as `Billing > Refunds`. Context for display, filtering and contextual embeddings.
Prepending chunk-level context (heading path or a generated summary) to the text that is embedded and indexed, keeping the original text for display.
Starting a new chunk where the embedding similarity between neighboring sentences drops. Costs an embedding per sentence and does not always beat structure-aware splitting.
